memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: As soon as he finished saying all this, the ground under them split apart and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, and all those associated with Korah, together with their possessions. They went down alive into the realm of the dead, with everything they owned; the earth closed over them, and they perished and were gone from the community. At their cries, all the Israelites around them fled, shouting, "The earth is going to swallow us too!" — Num 16:31-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The judgment falls exactly as Moses said. The ground splits, and the rebels go down. It is a terrible scene, and the surrounding Israelites flee in terror, crying out in fear. This is a moment of holy dread, when the reality of God's power to judge becomes undeniable.

We must not rush to explain away the horror of this. It is right to feel the weight of it. But it is meant to produce in us a healthy fear of the Lord — not a cringing terror, but a reverent awe that takes God seriously. The people fled shouting, suddenly aware that God is not to be trifled with. Sometimes we need such reminders to shake us out of our casual assumptions about God.

The fear of the Lord, Scripture says, is the beginning of wisdom. It is not opposed to loving God; it is part of loving Him rightly. To fear the Lord is to hold Him in the reverence He deserves, to know that He is holy, powerful, and not to be mocked. This awe is the soil in which true worship and humble obedience grow.

Yet for those who belong to Christ, this reverent fear is wrapped in love, not dread of condemnation. The same God whose power split the ground is the God who split the heavens to send His Son to save us. We stand before Him not as trembling rebels awaiting the earth to open, but as beloved children, because Christ absorbed the judgment we deserved. We can hold both truths together: awe at His holiness, and rest in His love. Let this scene deepen your reverence, and let the cross deepen your peace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you lost a healthy reverence and awe of God's holiness?
2. How is the fear of the Lord different from cringing terror?
3. How does the cross let you hold together awe of God and rest in His love?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, restore in me a healthy awe of Your holiness and power. Let the fear of the Lord be the beginning of wisdom in my life. Yet thank You that in Christ I come to You not as a trembling rebel but as a beloved child. Amen.
